- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates drops; increase downward bias or add early correction factor.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after spikes; apply lagged correction: subtract 1–2% of forecast from first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5%.
- Sentiment history with multiple 0.2 values suggests market is “overconfident”; model should be conservative, especially if true outcome shows volatility or reversal.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, model should be adjusted downward by 3–7% in next 7–10 days, regardless of sentiment.
